subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Tikal: Skyscraper City of the Maya
description: A fast breakdown of Tikal: Skyscraper City of the Maya for builders.

hook.text: A Maya city with skyscraper pyramids rising above the jungle canopy lay hidden in Guatemala for centuries.

buildup.text: Tikal housed up to 90,000 people and dominated the Maya lowlands from roughly 200 to 900 CE.

discovery.text: Temple IV rises 212 feet — the tallest pre-Columbian structure in the Americas. It was built around 741 CE.

twist.text: Tikal fought a bitter war with the rival city Calakmul. The conflict shaped Maya politics for centuries.

climax.text: LiDAR scans revealed 60,000 hidden structures around Tikal, showing the city was far larger than anyone imagined.

punchline.text: The jungle hid a city for a thousand years. Lasers found it in a day.

quiz.question: What did LiDAR technology reveal about Tikal?
options: The pyramids were built over natural rock formations
60,000 hidden structures showed the city was far larger than expected
Underground tunnels connected all major temples
